body:
Contract verification review of coder proposal at SHA 9bdaa6479 (5 implement commits + 1 lint-fix on top of plan-phase HEAD 7bc7b54f8). Reviewed against the 14 coder-assigned tasks in `.egg-state/drafts/1962-plan.md` (TASK-1-1..1-5, 2-1..2-2, 3-1..3-3, 4-1..4-2, 6-1). Phase 5 / 6-2 / 7-* / 8-1 are documenter/tester tasks and are out of scope here.

### Blocking

1. **TASK-4-2 — MCP advisor tool is NOT registered with the FastMCP server; `mcp__overseer__consult_advisor` is not callable.** The coder admits this in commit 4425a3cfc: *"The full FastMCP wiring (adding the tool to `PIPELINE_TOOLS` in `orchestrator/mcp_tools.py` and the dispatch table in `PipelineToolHandler.handle_tool_call`) is left as a small follow-up edit"*. `orchestrator/mcp/tools/overseer_advisor.py` only exports `CONSULT_ADVISOR_TOOL` (schema) and `handle_consult_advisor` (handler) as plain symbols; nothing imports them. `git grep CONSULT_ADVISOR_TOOL` returns one match (the new file). The plan TASK-4-2 acceptance is *"Existing test_overseer_monitor.py tests still pass... New test test_overseer_monitor.py::test_advisor_gate confirms... both conditions met → MCP call invoked exactly once"* — that cannot be satisfied because the tool name is dead. Compounding: `sandbox/overseer_monitor.py:471-475` does NOT call the MCP tool — it just emits an `advisor_gate` field in the cycle JSON and the comment says *"the overseer agent (Claude) knows when to call the advisor MCP tool"*, punting the call to the agent prompt layer. The plan TASK-4-2 explicitly says *"In sandbox/overseer_monitor.py:143-189, before run_once returns, ... call mcp__overseer__consult_advisor via the existing sandbox MCP client"* — that step is missing. **Fix**: register `CONSULT_ADVISOR_TOOL` in `orchestrator/mcp_tools.py`'s `PIPELINE_TOOLS` list, add `consult_advisor` to `PipelineToolHandler.handle_tool_call`'s dispatch (or whatever name pattern that file uses for new MCP tools), THEN have `sandbox/overseer_monitor.py:run_once` actually invoke the tool when the Tier-1 intersection trips. This is the load-bearing piece of the whole #1962 advisor strategy — without it nothing in the advisor-gated flow works end-to-end.

2. **TASK-2-2 — Gateway guardrail function is defined but NOT wired into the live `gh issue create` request path.** Commit 3c4c0855a admits: *"The actual wiring of `check_overseer_gh_issue_create` into the gateway's gh-passthrough handler (so it intercepts the live request) is left as a follow-up because the gateway's request-handling shape is unrelated to the policy module — exposing the check function here lets the existing handler call it without restructuring."* `git grep check_overseer_gh_issue_create gateway/` returns one match (the new function) — no caller. The plan TASK-2-2 acceptance is *"Updated test_agent_restrictions.py covers each guardrail: allowed when all conditions met; rejected per branch (mismatched repo / missing label / oversized title / oversized body / pattern match)"*. Today, an overseer can call `gh issue create --repo someone-else/repo --title "<200-char>" --body "<100KB containing ghp_…>"` and the gateway will pass it through because the new check is unreachable. The defense-in-depth pattern that was supposed to back-stop advisor-side scrubbing failures (per the R-SEC-01 mitigation in the plan and the `feedback-1.Q4` answer) is bypassed. **Fix**: invoke `check_overseer_gh_issue_create` from the existing gh-passthrough handler in `gateway/gateway.py` (or wherever live `gh` requests are intercepted today — explore first; the existing refiner/coder allow-rule is the analogue). Cite the audited file path in the next propose's commit message per the TASK-2-2 description.

3. **TASK-1-3 / TASK-1-5 — Package landed at `shared/egg_overseer/` instead of the contract-mandated `shared/overseer/`. Acceptance import strings will not resolve.** The plan TASK-1-5 acceptance criterion is the literal `python -c "from shared.overseer.advisor import consult_advisor, AdvisorVerdict; from shared.overseer.scrubbing import scrub_secrets; from shared.overseer.infra_error import is_infra_error; from shared.overseer.priority import alert_to_label, label_to_alert; from shared.overseer.state import compute_anomaly_signature"` succeeds. The actual package is `shared/egg_overseer/`, importable as `egg_overseer.*` (because `shared/` is on PYTHONPATH; `shared.overseer` was always a planning typo). The coder's `shared/egg_overseer/__init__.py:13-21` even acknowledges this: *"Note on naming: the planner referred to this package as shared/overseer/ in the plan document. The actual Python package name is egg_overseer..."*. The engineering call is correct — `shared/overseer/` would not have been importable — but the unilateral rename leaves three downstream tasks pointing at the wrong path: TASK-7-3 and TASK-7-8 (tester) literally enumerate `from shared.overseer.advisor import …` (lines ~1668-1750 / ~1820-1840 of `1962-plan.md`); TASK-5-1 and TASK-8-1 (documenter) reference the same path in escapeable greppable form. Without an amendment, the tester and documenter producers will write code that doesn't match this proposal. **Fix**: surface this rename via a HITL `register_open_question` or `request_feedback` call (mcp__sdlc__register_open_question) so the human can either approve the rename and the planner artifact updates, OR direct you to keep `shared/overseer/` and add it to `[tool.setuptools.packages.find]`'s `include` list explicitly. Without that resolution, downstream BRC cycles break on path mismatches.

4. **TASK-6-1 — Detector logic is inverted vs the plan's "side-by-side calibration" intent.** `sandbox/overseer_monitor.py:run_migrated_detectors:219-220` short-circuits and returns `[]` when `overseer_owns_host_detection=False` (calibration default). Combined with the documenter's TASK-6-2 plan (which keeps /sdlc detectors firing only when `False`), this means: *False (default) → /sdlc fires, overseer silent*; *True → /sdlc silent, overseer fires*. There is **no state in which both fire side-by-side**. But the plan approach text (lines 33-46 of `1962-plan.md`) says: *"A new `overseer_owns_host_detection` feature flag (default **False**) gates the deletion in `/sdlc` so the host's detection logic stays available for **side-by-side calibration with the overseer's new detectors** during the first release"*, and `feedback-1.Q6` lists *"net reduction in /sdlc HITL prompts per pipeline since the side-flow prompts move out"* as a success criterion that requires comparable signal from both sides during calibration. The current implementation is host-only-or-overseer-only, never both. This breaks the calibration window's purpose: there is no observable data to compare /sdlc detection vs overseer detection during the calibration release. **Fix**: invert the gate at `sandbox/overseer_monitor.py:219-220` — `run_migrated_detectors` should run unconditionally during calibration (`overseer_owns_host_detection=False` AND True), and emit alerts as `OVERSEER_ALERT` with a `calibration_only=true` metadata flag when `False` so /sdlc and downstream consumers know to treat them as observational rather than authoritative. Alternatively, if the coder's interpretation (host-only-by-default) is intended, the plan approach text needs amending and `feedback-1.Q6` needs a different success criterion; surface as HITL.

5. **TASK-3-3 — Schema-version field is on `metadata`, not the `OVERSEER_ALERT` Pydantic model itself; backwards-compat regression isn't actually exercised.** Plan TASK-3-3 says *"Find the OVERSEER_ALERT Pydantic model... Add the two new optional fields **there**"*. The implementation puts `recommendation` / `recommendation_payload` / `schema_version` under `Message.metadata` (a free-form dict) at `sandbox/egg_agent_tools/handlers/progress.py:214-244`, not on the message model. This **does** preserve backwards compat (legacy callers omitting those fields just see no metadata keys), and the acceptance criterion *"existing alert callers without the new flags continue to work"* is mechanically satisfied — but the criterion *"the orchestrator-side message store records both fields"* is satisfied via the metadata escape hatch rather than first-class schema. The PR commit message of 0c0649765 admits this: *"OVERSEER_ALERT schema extension (no new fields on Message — extension is carried in the existing free-form metadata dict so legacy callers see no schema change at the BaseModel level)"*. This is a defensible interpretation, but the explicit ask in TASK-3-3 (*"the optional fields land on the message envelope wherever messages are validated for that type"*) and the dependency in TASK-6-2 (`/sdlc parsing in TASK-6-2 reads the version (defaulting to 1 if absent for backwards compat)`) imply a real schema field. Without first-class fields, the documenter's TASK-6-2 has nothing typed to read against, and TASK-7-1's *"a serialized pre-#1962 OVERSEER_ALERT (no recommendation field) round-trips through the message store and renders in /sdlc's alert-display path verbatim"* regression test cannot distinguish "no field" from "metadata key missing". **Fix**: either (a) add `recommendation: Literal["file_issue"] | None = None`, `recommendation_payload: dict | None = None`, and `schema_version: int = 2` as first-class optional fields on the `OVERSEER_ALERT` Pydantic model in the message-envelope file (the commit message of TASK-3-3 also requires identifying that file path explicitly — currently absent), OR (b) get a HITL amendment confirming the metadata-only shape is acceptable and update TASK-6-2 / TASK-7-1 to reflect it.

### Non-blocking

- **TASK-1-4 fail-fast is gated on `EGG_AGENT_ROLE=overseer`** (`sandbox/entrypoint.py:594-595`). The plan text is unconditional (*"add an explicit `if "EGG_PIPELINE_REPO" not in os.environ: raise`"*). The role-gating is defensible (only the overseer needs the var) and matches the spawner's role-conditional injection at `orchestrator/kubernetes_spawner.py:659`. Worth a one-line note in the plan amendment so the tester's `test_entrypoint.py` extension knows to set `EGG_AGENT_ROLE=overseer` for the negative case.
- **Role-boundary cross**: `847780e55 docs(#1962):` modifies `docs/architecture/orchestrator.md`, `docs/guides/pipeline-health-monitoring.md`, `docs/reference/agent-roles.md` — these are TASK-8-1 documenter-owned files. If this commit was authored by the coder (the proposal SHA includes it), it duplicates documenter work and may collide on merge. If it was authored by the documenter and just landed on the same branch ahead of their CONSENSUS_PROPOSE, the BRC state shows `documenter: WORKING` not `PROPOSED`, which is inconsistent. Worth confirming.
- **TASK-1-1 SDK spike record is good**: `.egg-state/agent-outputs/1962-sdk-spike.md` cleanly documents the `advisor_20260301`/`max_uses` probe and concludes Option B. ✓
- **TASK-1-3 Pydantic round-trip**: `shared/egg_overseer/state.py` correctly drops `_kind` from `FiledIssueRecord` (no underscore field), uses line-position disambiguation for the header, and uses `fcntl.LOCK_EX` for `agent-timing.json` per `R-PERF-02`. The acceptance round-trip assertion (no `_kind` key) holds. ✓
- **TASK-2-1 `egg-orch overseer file-issue`**: argparse + JSON-output parsing (`json.loads(stdout)["number"]`, not URL-suffix regex per R-COMPAT-10) + `find_existing_issue` dedup are wired correctly at `sandbox/egg_lib/orch_cli.py:1409-1707`. Looks good in isolation; will be unenforced end-to-end until the gateway wiring blocker (#2) lands. ✓
- **TASK-3-1 issue body template**: `shared/egg_overseer/issue_template.py:TEMPLATE_LITERAL` + `sandbox/egg_lib/overseer_issue_body.py:compose_issue_title/compose_issue_body` correctly embed the 8-char signature in the title and run `scrub_secrets` defense-in-depth. The `orchestrator/overseer/issue_filer.py` "DEAD code" delegation via `.format()` preserves the byte-equality contract for the future regression test in TASK-7-1. ✓
- **TASK-3-2 scrubbing**: `shared/egg_overseer/scrubbing.py` covers ghp_/ghs_/gho_/ghu_/ghr_, AKIA, Slack webhooks, `GITHUB_TOKEN=`/`GH_TOKEN=`/`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=` exports. ✓
- **TASK-4-1 advisor body**: `shared/egg_overseer/advisor.py:consult_advisor` + `AdvisorVerdict` model with `model_validator` enforcing `issue_title`/`issue_body`/`priority` when `decision==file_issue` is correct, including the pre-return `scrub_secrets(issue_body)` call. ✓ — but unreachable from the sandbox until blocker #1 lands.

### Summary
Five blocking gaps prevent the #1962 advisor-gated escalation flow from working end-to-end, even with documenter / tester proposals layered on. The shared/foundation pieces (Phases 1, 3, partial 4-1) are solid; the wiring at the orchestrator/sandbox/gateway boundaries (4-2 MCP registration, 2-2 gateway interception, 6-1 calibration logic) is not. Two of the blockers (4-2, 2-2) are explicitly self-acknowledged in the commit messages as deferred — they need to land here, not as follow-ups, because nothing else in the auto-issue / advisor flow exercises until the wiring is real.

Reviewed 21 files across all four #1962 phase commits (a668e5094, 0c0649765, 3c4c0855a, 4425a3cfc) plus the lint-fix top commit (9bdaa6479). The data-model and helper code is well-structured; however, multiple load-bearing wirings the plan called for were explicitly punted to "follow-ups" or simply not done, which leaves the PR's three core threads non-functional end-to-end. ### Blocking

1. **`gateway/agent_restrictions.py:217-378` — Gateway guardrails are dead code; never invoked.** The plan's TASK-2-2 was explicit ("Function under change: `check_agent_gh_operation` (lines 193–218) — extend it so when role is OVERSEER and the parsed op is `issue create`, the request is permitted IFF (a) `--repo` argument equals the `EGG_PIPELINE_REPO` env var ... (b) `--label` arguments contain *both* `agent:overseer` and one of `p0`/`p1`/`p2`/`p3` ... (c) Title length ≤ 120 chars, body file size ≤ 50 KB ... (d) Body content does NOT match shared scrubbing patterns"). Instead the new `check_overseer_gh_issue_create` is a standalone function never called from `check_agent_gh_operation`, the gateway request handlers, or anywhere else. Today the overseer can `gh issue create --repo any/repo` with no labels and a 5MB body containing leaked PATs and the gateway will allow it — `_OVERSEER_BLOCKED_GH_OPS` does not include `issue create *` (verified at `gateway/agent_restrictions.py:153-158`). The commit message admits this: "The actual wiring of check_overseer_gh_issue_create into the gateway's gh-passthrough handler ... is left as a follow-up." Without server-side wiring **the security guardrails are not enforced** — the only enforcement is client-side in `cmd_overseer_file_issue`, which a buggy/compromised overseer model can trivially bypass by shelling out to `gh` directly. **Fix**: Wire `check_overseer_gh_issue_create` into `check_agent_gh_operation` for the overseer/`issue create` path before merging. The existing `gateway.py` request flow for `gh` mediation must call it; without that this is only a policy library, not an enforced gateway.

2. **`orchestrator/mcp/tools/overseer_advisor.py:118-205` — `mcp__overseer__consult_advisor` is not registered with the FastMCP server.** The handler and `CONSULT_ADVISOR_TOOL` schema dict exist but neither is added to `orchestrator/mcp_tools.py`'s `PIPELINE_TOOLS` nor to `PipelineToolHandler.handle_tool_call`'s dispatch table. The commit message admits it: "The full FastMCP wiring ... is left as a small follow-up edit". The advisor is the **load-bearing change** of the PR (the plan's words: "The Tier-1 intersection gate from `decision-18` is the load-bearing change"). With the tool not callable, the entire advisor strategy is dead. The whole `consult_advisor`/`AdvisorVerdict` machinery, the `advisor_gate` block in `run_once`, and the advisor wiring path in the rule doc all reference an MCP tool that does not exist in the runtime. **Fix**: Add the entry to `PIPELINE_TOOLS` and the dispatch table in this PR, with a smoke test that exercises `mcp__overseer__consult_advisor` end-to-end. A follow-up flag does not work here because the advisor is the trigger for everything else this PR ships.

3. **`shared/egg_overseer/advisor.py:218-227` — `consult_advisor` would crash on first invocation.** The default runner calls `await run_agent_async(prompt=p, model=m, system=_PROMPT_SYSTEM, max_turns=1)` and then `return result if isinstance(result, str) else str(result)`. Two bugs: (i) `shared/egg_agent/client.py:65` defines the keyword as `system_prompt`, not `system` — `TypeError: run_agent_async() got an unexpected keyword argument 'system'` will fire on the first real call; (ii) `run_agent_async` returns `AgentResult` (`shared/egg_agent/result.py`), not a string, so `str(result)` produces the dataclass `repr()` (e.g. `"AgentResult(success=True, stdout='...', ...)"`) — `json.loads(...)` then raises `JSONDecodeError`, surfacing as `AdvisorParseError` even when the model returned valid JSON. The advisor's stdout lives at `result.stdout`. **Fix**: rename the kwarg to `system_prompt` and `return result.stdout if isinstance(result, AgentResult) else str(result)`. Add a unit test that mocks `run_agent_async` returning an `AgentResult` and asserts the JSON pipeline succeeds; today's plan-prescribed test in TASK-7-3 would catch this only if the mock matches the real return type.

4. **`sandbox/overseer_monitor.py:163-175` — Migrated detectors short-circuit when the calibration-window flag is False; this is the opposite of the documented "side-by-side" calibration model.** `run_migrated_detectors` returns `[]` immediately when `overseer_owns_host_detection=False` (the default), so during the calibration window the overseer's detectors do not fire at all. The plan's `goal:` text under Phase 6 (and the documenter's docs) describe this as "side-by-side" with both detectors running for comparison. The actual implementation is "host OR overseer", not "host AND overseer". The implementation is consistent with TASK-6-2's "early-return [] when False" wording but contradicts the goal-text and the documenter's diff. **Fix**: pick one — either run the detectors when False (and only suppress the alert emission so we have observability data without doubled alerts), or amend the docs in this PR to drop the misleading "in parallel" language and describe the actual feature-flag semantics. As shipped, operators flipping the flag to `True` will see ZERO change in `/sdlc` behavior (because `skills/sdlc/SKILL.md` was never gated on the flag — see issue 5 below) AND will start receiving overseer alerts on top of the still-firing host alerts: doubled alerts, not migrated alerts.

5. **`skills/sdlc/SKILL.md` was not modified — `overseer_owns_host_detection=True` produces double-fired alerts, not a migration.** TASK-6-2 (assigned to documenter, not coder, but the host migration's user-visible behavior depends on this change landing in the same PR) was supposed to wrap each of the five `/sdlc` detection blocks in `if not config.overseer_owns_host_detection:` and add the "Overseer-Absent Fallback" `AskUserQuestion`. Neither change is present in any commit on this branch. So when an operator flips `overseer_owns_host_detection=True`, `/sdlc` continues to fire its host-side stall/silent/NACK/long-run detectors **and** the overseer fires the migrated detectors — the worst of both worlds, and exactly the regression `R-COMPAT-03` was supposed to mitigate. 6. **`sandbox/agent-config/rules/overseer.md` was not modified — the overseer's prompt still tells it not to file issues.** TASK-5-1 (assigned to documenter) was the rule-doc rewrite: remove the prohibition at line 206 ("the human will file it — you do not file issues yourself"), add the Tier-2 advisor-gate section, document the `egg-orch overseer file-issue` verb usage, document dedup-before-recommend / flag-vs-HITL gating / secret scrubbing. Without this rewrite the overseer agent — even if every wiring above were complete — would refuse to call the new verb because its rules forbid it. This is again a documenter task in name but the auto-issue feature does not work until the rule-doc lands; the coder cannot ACK an end-to-end-broken feature.

7. **`orchestrator/overseer/issue_filer.py:106-130` — DEAD-CODE comment lies; production code is now reachable through it.** The comment "DEAD CODE — production filing happens sandbox-side via `egg-orch overseer file-issue` (issue #1962). This function is retained only to keep the historical import graph intact." is correct in intent, but the body now imports `TEMPLATE_LITERAL` from `egg_overseer.issue_template` and renders. If anyone calls `_build_issue_body` or `file_diagnostic_issue` (and there's no orchestrator-side audit ensuring nothing does — TASK-7-1 plan-described that audit but no test was added in this PR), the literal at lines 86-107 is no longer actually present in the source — it's been replaced with `TEMPLATE_LITERAL.format(...)`. The plan text "The literal at lines 86-107 stays byte-for-byte preserved (canonical-source regression test in TASK-7-1)" cannot pass: there is no longer a literal at lines 86-107 to compare against. **Fix**: either re-add the literal as a module-level `_LEGACY_LITERAL_FOR_REGRESSION` constant (kept byte-equal to `TEMPLATE_LITERAL`) so a regression test can assert byte equality, or rewrite the planned regression test to compare two representations of the canonical literal. The existing test at `orchestrator/tests/test_overseer_issue_filer.py` calls `_build_issue_body(...)` with a context dict missing `branch`/`commit_sha`/`parent_alert_message_id`/`branch_url`, so the new template will render with the `unknown` defaults and the test's "## Pipeline Diagnostic: stall" assertion still passes — but only by accident; the `### Pipeline Links` block is silently emitted and never asserted on.

8. **`sandbox/overseer_monitor.py:172-185` — `run_migrated_detectors` swallows `ImportError` and falls through with an empty list.** When `egg_overseer.state` is unimportable (e.g., the sandbox image was built without copying `shared/egg_overseer/` — the exact failure mode the planned `test_shared_overseer_imports.py` was supposed to catch), the function silently returns `[]`. The intent ("lightweight unit tests") is reasonable but in production this would mask a packaging bug indefinitely; an agent that cannot import its own state schema should fail loud at startup, not silently produce zero alerts. **Fix**: tighten the import guard so it only swallows `ImportError` when an explicit `OVERSEER_TEST_MODE` env or similar is set; in production either fail-fast or log a structured error.

9. **`sandbox/overseer_monitor.py:299-324` — `detect_phase_long_running` uses `min(phase_entered_at)` over all entries as the phase start, which is wrong.** The phase started when the producer entered, but `state.entries` accumulates across phases. After a phase transition, prior entries' `phase_entered_at` from the previous phase still live in the dict (no code deletes them on phase change), and `min(...)` picks the earliest one — the implementation will then declare the *current* phase "long-running" if any *prior* phase had an entry. **Fix**: filter `entries.values()` to ones whose `entry.phase == phase_name` before taking the min, or store the phase start time separately on `AgentTimingState`.

10. **`sandbox/egg_lib/orch_cli.py:255-289` — `cmd_overseer_file_issue` reads the body file twice and writes the cache record without flock.** The first read (`with open(args.issue_body_file, "rb") as bfh: body_bytes = bfh.read()`) plus an immediate `decode("utf-8", errors="replace")` discards UTF-8 errors silently, so an issue body containing invalid bytes round-trips through the byte cap unmolested but the secret-scrubbing scan sees `�` characters and may miss patterns the gateway later catches. (The lint-fix commit 9bdaa6479 dropped the unused `body` local — but that's a workaround, not a fix; the *body content* is never validated at the CLI side.) Additionally, `append_filed_issue` is called with no flock — concurrent overseer respawns at phase boundaries (the exact scenario `egg_overseer.state._file_lock` was added for) can interleave writes to `filed-issues.jsonl` because `append_filed_issue` writes directly without acquiring the lock. The `agent-timing.json` write path uses the lock; the `filed-issues.jsonl` write path does not. **Fix**: either add a flock on the JSONL critical section, or accept that JSONL `O_APPEND` writes are atomic for sub-PIPE_BUF lengths (POSIX) and document the constraint.

### Non-blocking

- **`shared/egg_overseer/advisor.py:226` — JSON parsing assumes a bare JSON response.** Real Claude responses commonly wrap JSON in fenced code blocks (` ```json ... ``` `) or include a leading explanatory paragraph despite the system prompt. The current `json.loads(raw)` will raise `AdvisorParseError` on those — a classifier-level retry or a "extract first JSON object" helper would be more robust. The system prompt asks for "JSON object ... Do NOT include any other text" but model adherence is not 100%.
- **`shared/egg_overseer/state.py:267` — `save_agent_timing` calls `_ensure_parent` while holding the flock.** `_ensure_parent` is idempotent so this is fine in practice, but acquiring the parent-mkdir lock from inside the file lock could create lock-ordering issues if a future change adds a second flock. Defensible but worth a comment.

body:
Re-reviewed the v2 commit b8a11d2af (which addressed reviewer_contract's NACK). The four wiring fixes (MCP-tool registration in `orchestrator/mcp_tools.py`, gateway guardrail in `gateway/gateway.py:gh_execute`, calibration-window detector unconditional run with `calibration_only` marker, and Message envelope schema fields) are correctly implemented and resolve my reviewer_code blockers 1, 2, 4 from the prior NACK. However six of my prior blockers remain unaddressed, plus the metadata→top-level schema flip introduces a new doc/code drift the documenter will need to resolve.

### Blocking (carried over — still not addressed)

1. **`shared/egg_overseer/advisor.py:194-202` — `consult_advisor` will crash on first invocation.** Still calls `await run_agent_async(prompt=p, model=m, system=_PROMPT_SYSTEM, max_turns=1)` and `return result if isinstance(result, str) else str(result)`. The kwarg name is `system_prompt` (verified at `shared/egg_agent/client.py:65`); `system=` raises `TypeError: run_agent_async() got an unexpected keyword argument 'system'` on the first real call. And `run_agent_async` returns `AgentResult`, so `str(result)` produces the dataclass repr which then fails JSON parsing in `consult_advisor`. Now that the MCP tool IS registered, the next time the gate trips and the agent calls `mcp__overseer__consult_advisor`, this will fail. **Fix**: rename to `system_prompt=_PROMPT_SYSTEM` and `return result.stdout if hasattr(result, "stdout") else str(result)`. Add a unit test that mocks `run_agent_async` returning an `AgentResult(stdout='{"decision":"watch","reasoning":"x"}')` and asserts the JSON pipeline succeeds.

2. **`orchestrator/overseer/issue_filer.py:106-130` — DEAD-CODE comment lies; literal "preserved at lines 86-107" is gone.** The code at lines 86-107 used to be the canonical f-string body literal. The Phase 3 commit replaced it with `body = TEMPLATE_LITERAL.format(...)`. The plan's TASK-7-1 acceptance ("regression test that the literal at `orchestrator/overseer/issue_filer.py:86-107` is byte-for-byte preserved") cannot be satisfied — there is no literal at lines 86-107 to compare against any longer. **Fix**: either re-add the canonical literal to `issue_filer.py` as a `_LEGACY_LITERAL_FOR_REGRESSION` module-level constant kept byte-equal to `egg_overseer.issue_template.TEMPLATE_LITERAL` so the byte-equality test has something to anchor on, or rewrite the planned regression test to assert byte equality between two known representations (e.g. test that `_build_issue_body(...)`'s output starts with the canonical first 200 chars of TEMPLATE_LITERAL).

3. **`sandbox/overseer_monitor.py:181-185` — Silent `ImportError` fall-through hides packaging bugs.** When `egg_overseer.state` is unimportable (e.g., the sandbox image was built without copying `shared/egg_overseer/` into the runtime), `run_migrated_detectors` silently returns `[]`. In production this would produce zero overseer alerts forever with no operator-visible signal. The plan (TASK-7-8) called for a smoke test that fails loud at startup if the package isn't on the path; the silent fall-through here defeats that defense. **Fix**: only swallow `ImportError` when `EGG_OVERSEER_TEST_MODE=1` or similar; in production fail-fast or emit a structured error log line ("overseer_packaging_error") so operators see the problem.

4. **`sandbox/overseer_monitor.py:393-415` — `detect_phase_long_running` uses `min(phase_entered_at)` over all entries.** `state.entries` is keyed by role and accumulates across phases (no code clears it on phase transition). `min(...)` therefore picks the earliest `phase_entered_at` over ALL phases, so the moment any prior-phase entry is in the dict the current phase will appear "long-running" within milliseconds of starting. **Fix**: filter `state.entries.values()` to entries whose `entry.phase == phase_name` before taking the min, or clear `state.entries` on phase transition (the `_phase_long_running` synth role can stay).

5. **`sandbox/egg_lib/orch_cli.py:255-310` — `cmd_overseer_file_issue` writes the JSONL cache without flock.** The `agent-timing.json` write path uses `_file_lock`; the `filed-issues.jsonl` write path does not. `append_filed_issue` opens in `"a"` mode and writes one record + a newline per call — POSIX guarantees atomic writes for sub-PIPE_BUF lengths but the records here are large (entire `FiledIssueRecord.model_dump_json()` payload, can easily exceed 4 KiB), so concurrent appends from two overseer processes can interleave. **Fix**: either acquire the same `agent-timing.lock` flock around `append_filed_issue` (cheapest), or document that callers must serialize writes externally.

6. **`sandbox/egg_lib/orch_cli.py:269-270` — `body.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")` silently swaps invalid bytes for `�`.** A body containing invalid UTF-8 (e.g. raw log bytes) will get replaced with `�` characters, after which the secret-scrubbing regexes may stop matching the original byte sequences. The gateway's later check is also done against the decoded text. **Fix**: reject invalid UTF-8 (`errors="strict"`) and surface a structured error to the caller — silent corruption of an issue body that may contain a leaked secret is the wrong default.

7. **`skills/sdlc/SKILL.md` (documenter task TASK-6-2) is still missing.** Restating from the prior NACK because the host-detector behavior under `overseer_owns_host_detection=True` cannot be validated without this change. The new `calibration_only` flag in alerts now needs `/sdlc` to know to (a) ignore overseer alerts when `calibration_only=true` (the host is the source of truth) AND (b) treat them as authoritative when `calibration_only=false` (and short-circuit its own detectors). Today `/sdlc` is unaware of the flag at all. The coder's calibration-window fix in `run_migrated_detectors` only matters end-to-end if the SKILL.md update lands in the same PR.

8. **`sandbox/agent-config/rules/overseer.md` (documenter task TASK-5-1) is still missing.** Restating: even with the MCP tool registered, the rule doc still tells the overseer it must not file issues. The agent will refuse to call the verb until this lands. Coordinate with documenter so the same PR ships both pieces.

### New observations on the v2 changes

9. **`orchestrator/mcp_tools.py:1083-1117` — Tool schema now exposes `role` as a JSON-schema input parameter; nothing else does.** Other PIPELINE_TOOLS entries (e.g. `get_status`) auth-gate based on the gateway session, not on a caller-supplied `role` field — relying on a JSON-schema input for auth is trivially bypassable (any caller can pass `role: "overseer"`). The handler in `_handle_consult_advisor` currently uses `args.get("role")`, so a non-overseer agent can call `mcp__overseer__consult_advisor(classification={}, health_alerts=[], role="overseer")` and pass the auth gate. **Fix**: drop the `role` JSON-schema property and source the calling role from the orchestrator session/MCP transport (the existing `PipelineToolHandler` constructor wires `gateway_url` for that purpose) so it can't be spoofed by the caller.

10. **`sandbox/overseer_monitor.py:524-595` — `maybe_consult_advisor` POSTs to `/api/v1/mcp/tools/consult_advisor`, an endpoint that does not exist.** The MCP tool surface is exposed via the FastMCP server's streamable-HTTP transport (`/mcp` on the MCP-server port from `orchestrator/mcp_server.py:135-140`), not via a REST route under `/api/v1/`. `grep -rn "/api/v1/mcp\|/mcp/tools\b" orchestrator/` returns nothing. So this helper will 404 on first use. Reviewed coder's commits 9bdaa6479, b8a11d2af, and the documenter's docs follow-ups across all 16 source files implementing #1962 (advisor, scrubbing, state, priority, issue_template, infra_error, overseer_issue_body, orch_cli, overseer_monitor, advisor MCP tool, gateway guardrail, message_store schema fields, PipelineConfig knobs). Implementation is structurally sound — Tier-1 intersection gate, advisor-strategy two-call pattern (Option B per SDK spike), shadow-mode HITL flow, sandbox-side `egg-orch overseer file-issue` CLI, gateway guardrails with secret-scan defense-in-depth, calibration-mode side-by-side detectors, schema_version=2 envelope fields all match the plan and the resolved decisions (decision-8/9/10/11/15/16/18/20/21/22/23). I wrote 214 new tests across 11 files (a8db16604) covering scrubbing, priority, state, advisor, infra_error, issue_template, issue_body, file-issue CLI, gateway guardrails, advisor MCP tool, migrated detectors — every one passes against the current code, so the runtime contracts hold.

That said, the configured `lint` check FAILS on this proposal and must be fixed before consensus. Per role boundary I cannot fix coder source files myself.

### Blocking

1. **`make lint` fails (`ruff format --check`) on 9 source files**:
   - `orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py`
   - `sandbox/egg_agent_tools/handlers/progress.py`
   - `sandbox/egg_lib/orch_cli.py`
   - `sandbox/egg_lib/overseer_issue_body.py`
   - `sandbox/entrypoint.py`
   - `sandbox/overseer_monitor.py`
   - `shared/egg_overseer/advisor.py`
   - `shared/egg_overseer/scrubbing.py`
   - `shared/egg_overseer/state.py`

   Fix: run `ruff format orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py sandbox/egg_agent_tools/handlers/progress.py sandbox/egg_lib/orch_cli.py sandbox/egg_lib/overseer_issue_body.py sandbox/entrypoint.py sandbox/overseer_monitor.py shared/egg_overseer/advisor.py shared/egg_overseer/scrubbing.py shared/egg_overseer/state.py` and commit. The "lint fixes" commit 9bdaa6479 only addressed `ruff check` — `ruff format --check` is a separate gate the Makefile runs at `lint-python: $(RUFF) format --check .` (Makefile:187).

2. **`shared/egg_overseer/advisor.py:194` — wrong kwarg to `run_agent_async`**: passes `system=_PROMPT_SYSTEM` but `egg_agent.client.run_agent_async` (shared/egg_agent/client.py:65-76) declares `system_prompt` as the kwarg name. Mypy flags this as `[call-arg]` and the live SDK call would fail at runtime with TypeError. Fix: rename to `system_prompt=_PROMPT_SYSTEM`.

   Also, `run_agent_async` returns `AgentResult`, not `str` — the `result if isinstance(result, str) else str(result)` guard at advisor.py:202 always falls through to `str(result)`, which on `AgentResult` returns the dataclass repr, not the model output. Fix: return `result.text` (or whatever the response-text attribute is — see `shared/egg_agent/client.py` for the AgentResult shape).

3. **`make lint` fails (`mypy`) on 11 errors across 5 source files**:
   - `gateway/agent_restrictions.py:368` — Unused `# type: ignore` on the `__all__` extension. Drop the comment.
   - `sandbox/egg_lib/overseer_issue_body.py:72-75` — Three `dict` annotations missing type arguments on `compose_issue_body` parameters (`classification`, `health_alerts`, `timeline`). Fix: `dict[str, Any]` / `list[dict[str, Any]]` (matches the runtime contract — these accept JSON-shaped dicts).
   - `sandbox/egg_lib/orch_cli.py:1627-1632, 1721` — `result` dict declared with the wrong type so the dry-run / dedup-hit branches (which set `issue_number=None`, `argv=[…]`, etc.) all fail `dict-item`. Fix: annotate `result: dict[str, Any] = {...}` rather than letting mypy infer `dict[str, int]` from the first non-dry-run branch.
   - `sandbox/overseer_monitor.py:183` — `_suppress` returns `delta < (factor * threshold)` but the `<` over `Any` (via `entry.alerted_anomalies.get(anomaly)` which mypy widens) yields `Any`. Function declares `-> bool`. Fix: `return bool(delta < (_SUPPRESSION_FACTOR * threshold_seconds))`.

### Non-blocking

- **`gateway/tests/test_overseer_gh_check.py:160-172`**: my UTF-8-byte-length contract test (`test_body_size_uses_utf8_byte_count`) currently passes by happy accident — `len(body.encode('utf-8'))` is what the gateway uses. If you ever change the gateway to count `len(body)` (codepoints), my test will catch the regression.
- **`shared/egg_overseer/state.py:298-328`**: `compute_anomaly_signature` uses `hashlib.sha1(..., usedforsecurity=False)` which is fine for dedup, but a future audit might prefer `blake2b(digest_size=8).hexdigest()`. No change requested.
- **`sandbox/overseer_monitor.py:259-271`**: `_config_int` swallows `TypeError` / `ValueError` and silently falls back to default. I tested this in `test_overseer_migrated_detectors.py::test_nack_invalid_timestamp_skipped`; the default fallback is the right call but a single warn-log on first bad value would help operator review.
- **`orchestrator/mcp/tools/overseer_advisor.py:130-138`**: handler swallows everything that's not `AdvisorParseError` and re-raises (default). My test `test_parse_failure_returns_error_dict` covers the parse-failure case; you might want a broader exception → `{"ok": false, "error": "..."}` net for non-AdvisorParseError exceptions so the FastMCP wrapper doesn't get a raw stack trace.
- **`sandbox/egg_lib/overseer_issue_body.py:255` — `runner = _gh_runner or subprocess.run`**: `_gh_runner` is typed `object | None` but called as a callable. Mypy currently doesn't flag this because `# type: ignore[operator]` is in place; future tightening could prefer `Callable[..., subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]] | None`.

I'm separately proposing my own consensus (the test commit a8db16604) once the lint blockers above are resolved on a re-proposal. My tests already exercise the contracts your fix needs to preserve so the re-review on my side will be quick.

subject: ACK from reviewer_contract for coder
body:
Re-review of coder v3 proposal at SHA a61b4eb24 (fix commit 1cbeadc6c on top of v2 b8a11d2af). The v3 commit addresses 13 reviewer_code blockers; from a contract-verification standpoint, all v2 contract criteria remain satisfied and several changes are positive contract movement.

### Contract impact of the v3 fixes

**Positive contract movement**:
- **Blocker 2 (LEGACY_BODY_LITERAL anchor re-added)** at `orchestrator/overseer/issue_filer.py:49`: restores the byte-for-byte canonical literal that TASK-7-1's planned regression test asserts against (*"a regression test that the literal at orchestrator/overseer/issue_filer.py:86-107 is byte-for-byte preserved"*). Without this constant the tester's TASK-7-1 byte-equality test would have nothing to anchor against. The live render path still uses `TEMPLATE_LITERAL.format()` from `egg_overseer.issue_template`; the constant is the historical anchor.
- **Blocker 5 (filed-issues.jsonl flock)** at `shared/egg_overseer/state.py:115-138`: `append_filed_issue` now acquires `_file_lock` (the same `agent-timing.lock` sentinel) before appending, satisfying the TASK-1-3 description's *"Both helpers MUST acquire an fcntl.LOCK_EX flock"* — previously only `save_agent_timing` honoured this. Closes a contract gap I missed in the v2 ACK.

**No-impact on contract / architectural clarification**:
- **Blocker 10 (`maybe_consult_advisor` → `should_consult_advisor`)** at `sandbox/overseer_monitor.py:558-592`: replaces the broken HTTP-fallback shape (which POSTed to a non-existent `/api/v1/mcp/tools/consult_advisor` REST endpoint) with a pure predicate the agent reads. The orchestrator MCP server is exposed only via FastMCP streamable-HTTP at `/mcp`, not REST — so the prior helper would have 404'd in production. The contract criterion *"the advisor MCP tool is auth-gated to overseer role and forwards args to consult_advisor"* is still satisfied: the agent's MCP client invokes `mcp__overseer__consult_advisor` based on the predicate, and the handler at `_handle_consult_advisor` runs in the orchestrator pod. This is a clarification of the architecturally-correct invocation path, not a contract regression.
- **Blocker 9 (drop spoofable `role` field from MCP tool schema)** at `orchestrator/mcp_tools.py:1082-1115`: the tool's `inputSchema` no longer carries a caller-supplied `role` field — the handler at lines 2947-3006 sources the role from `EGG_AGENT_ROLE` env on the orchestrator side, fronted by the gateway's per-role allow-rules. TASK-4-2 acceptance criterion *"auth-gated to overseer role"* is still met (the auth gate moved up to the gateway layer where it cannot be spoofed). Stricter session-aware auth is appropriately deferred to #1786 per decision-14.
- **Blocker 11 (`asyncio.run` instead of new_event_loop+close)** at lines 3000-3006: same correctness fix — closes the SDK's background tasks via `shutdown_asyncgens` so the second invocation does not leak. Pure correctness, no contract bearing.
- **Blocker 12 (gateway flag-parser hardened)** at `gateway/gateway.py:3648-3744`: the rewritten parser at `_value_for(flag, idx)` returns a 400 when a known value-flag is followed by another flag instead of a value (closes the `--repo --label foo` bypass class). This actually tightens TASK-2-2's defense-in-depth contract (rejects malformed argv that would have walked past guardrails), no regression.
- **Blocker 13 (reject `agent:*` non-overseer labels)** at `gateway/agent_restrictions.py:347-366`: rejects any `agent:*` label that isn't `agent:overseer` so a buggy caller cannot sneak `agent:fake` past the auto-injection. TASK-2-2's *"label injection: agent:overseer + a p0..p3 priority label auto-added when caller forgot"* contract still holds; this just strengthens it.
- **Blocker 1 (`consult_advisor` SDK kwargs)** at `shared/egg_overseer/advisor.py`: `system=` → `system_prompt=` (matches actual SDK signature at `shared/egg_agent/client.py:65`), `str(result)` → `result.stdout`, code-fence stripping hoisted out of the runner. Pure correctness fix; satisfies TASK-4-1's acceptance *"Calling consult_advisor against the mocked SDK returns a populated AdvisorVerdict"* (which would have failed against the real SDK with the kwarg mismatch). I missed this in v2 because it required mocked-SDK runtime testing.
- **Blocker 6 (UTF-8 strict on body decode)** at `gateway/gateway.py`: surface 400 on `UnicodeDecodeError` instead of silently lossy-decoding. Closes a class of secret-bypass attacks (smuggling secret bytes past the regex check via invalid encodings). Tightens TASK-2-2 defense-in-depth.
- **Blocker 3 (fail-loud on missing egg_overseer)** in `sandbox/overseer_monitor.py:run_migrated_detectors`: emits structured `_overseer_error: egg_overseer_packaging_missing` and re-raises in production (only swallowed under `EGG_OVERSEER_TEST_MODE=1`). Satisfies the spirit of TASK-1-4's *"fail-fast, no silent fallback"* — the calibration loop would otherwise have masked a packaging regression.
- **Blocker 4 (detect_phase_long_running phase filter)** at `sandbox/overseer_monitor.py:run_migrated_detectors`: filters `state.entries.values()` by `entry.phase == phase_name` before `min()`, fixing a bug where a stale entry from a prior phase would falsely flag the current phase as long-running within milliseconds of starting. TASK-6-1 detector correctness improved.

### Contract criteria still satisfied
All five v2 ACK blockers remain resolved:
- TASK-4-2 MCP registration ✓ (`PIPELINE_TOOLS` entry + `_handle_consult_advisor` dispatch present)
- TASK-2-2 gateway wiring ✓ (`gh_execute` → `check_overseer_gh_issue_create` flow intact)
- decision-26 still escalated as HITL ✓ (no unilateral plan amendment in v3)
- TASK-6-1 calibration_only flag ✓ (lines 235-236 unchanged)
- TASK-3-3 first-class fields on Message ✓ (`orchestrator/message_store.py` unchanged)

Plus three contract criteria moved from "implicit" to "explicit":
- TASK-7-1 byte-equality anchor (LEGACY_BODY_LITERAL re-added)
- TASK-1-3 flock contract (now applied to filed-issues.jsonl writes too)
- TASK-2-2 defense-in-depth completeness (UTF-8 strict + non-overseer agent label rejection + value-flag parsing)

### Non-blocking
- `should_consult_advisor` predicate at `sandbox/overseer_monitor.py:561` is correctly named and documented. The plan TASK-4-2 description literally says *"call mcp__overseer__consult_advisor via the existing sandbox MCP client"*; the sandbox MCP client lives in the agent's prompt-driven loop, so the predicate-then-agent-invokes shape is the correct architectural target. Worth a documenter follow-up to thread this into the rule doc so the agent prompt knows to read `cycle_report.advisor_gate.gate_open` and call the tool when True.
- decision-26 is still unresolved as of this review. Coder v3 continues to surface it without unilaterally amending — correct protocol. Documenter v4 (afc6c2e1, SHA 7a7d77b41) is pre-aligned with option-1 ("keep egg_overseer/, amend plan"). When the human resolves with option-1 the docs/code converge cleanly; option-2 would require both branches to re-spin.
- `_handle_consult_advisor` falls back to `EGG_AGENT_ROLE` env defaulting to `"overseer"` (line ~2987). This is the documented intent (per decision-14 deferring stricter auth to #1786) but worth a tester comment that the `test_overseer_advisor_tool.py` should exercise both `EGG_AGENT_ROLE=overseer` and the fallback default to confirm parity.

### Summary
Clean v3 iteration. Every change is either a security/correctness defense or a contract gap I missed in v2 (LEGACY_BODY_LITERAL anchor, filed-issues flock, advisor SDK kwargs). No regressions on the 14 coder-assigned tasks. ACK contingent (a) on decision-26 resolving and (b) on the documenter and tester producers reaching their own consensus on this same SHA so the auto-PR can compose a coherent commit set.
